resources.string: Extras that make the Pad work with the rest of your devices
Playing or calling on the Pad moves your AirPods to it, and playing on your iPhone or Mac moves them back. Restarts Bluetooth when changed.
Needs the ALXP Bluetooth patch in this ROM
Shows your iPhone notifications on the Pad. Pair once from the iPhone: Settings > Bluetooth > %1$s.
Copy on the Pad, paste on your Mac, and back. Text and images, over your Wi-Fi with ALXP for Mac.
Use the Pad as an extra Mac display, like Sidecar. Start it from ALXP for Mac; touch and the pen move the pointer.
Shows your iPhone notifications on the Pad, the way a smartwatch gets them. You can answer or dismiss them from here too.
Pair your AirPods with the Pad once: open the case near the Pad, hold the button on the back until the light flashes white, then pick them in Bluetooth settings.
Turn on the switch above. Bluetooth restarts once so the AirPods see the Pad as an Apple device.
Play music or take a call on the Pad: the AirPods move to the Pad.
Play on your iPhone or Mac: the AirPods move back. The status above shows which AirPods the Pad is following.
Turn on the switch above and allow the permissions it asks for.
On the iPhone, open Settings > Bluetooth and tap %1$s under Other Devices.
Accept the pairing code on both, then tap Allow when the iPhone asks to share notifications.
The status above changes to Working. New iPhone notifications now appear on the Pad.
On the Mac, build and open ALXP for Mac: run mac/make-app.sh from the ALXP Parts source, then open mac/build/ALXP.app. Turn on Open at Login in its menu.
Keep the Pad and the Mac on the same Wi-Fi, or connect them with USB with USB debugging on.
The first time, the ALXP menu on the Mac shows a pairing code and the Pad asks to pair. Check that the code matches and tap Pair.
Copy text or an image on one device and paste it on the other. The status above shows Working while the Mac is linked.
On the Mac, allow ALXP in System Settings > Privacy & Security for Screen Recording and Accessibility.
In the ALXP menu on the Mac, choose Use Pad as Display. The Pad shows the extra screen; touch and the pen move the pointer.
AirPods switching is based on LibrePods.
